title: A Life Grid Shows a Chosen Timeline, Not Your Expiry Date
description: Read a life grid as a chosen timeline based on your settings. Use years, months or weeks for reflection without treating empty squares as a lifespan prediction.
direct: A life grid counts weeks, months or years against a lifespan you choose. Use it to think about how you want to spend your time.

cards.choice.heading: Start with the decision
cards.choice.body: The same birthday can produce different remaining space when the chosen lifespan changes. That does not mean your health or future changed. The display is a way to reflect on priorities, and its assumptions should stay visible in how you interpret it.
sections.detail-0.heading: Do not turn the grid into a score
sections.detail-0.body: A filled square does not judge whether a week was valuable, productive or wasted. A timeline cannot account for everything that happened in it. You can use a coarser view or set it aside if the display is unhelpful. Optional reminders are a separate choice; there is no need to enable notifications to use the app.
sections.detail-1.heading: What the app actually offers
sections.detail-1.body: It combines the life grid with Screen Time app blocking and optional reminders. The current listing explicitly describes the countdown as a reflection tool, not a medical assessment or a death prediction. One scheduled rule and unlimited thirty-minute Block Now sessions are free; Pro adds more scheduled rules.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Why did my remaining grid change after I edited my lifespan setting?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: The grid recalculates against your new endpoint. The change reflects an input choice, so use it as a planning view.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Does an individual square represent a predicted date?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: A square represents the unit you selected, such as a week or year, within the timeline you set. It is not a health estimate.

steps.step-1.text: In Dying Soon: Screen Time Limit, review your birthday and selected lifespan before reading the life grid.
steps.step-2.text: Choose a years, months or weeks view that helps you reflect. Treat the remaining space as a planning perspective rather than an individual forecast.
steps.step-3.text: Pick one concrete activity you want to make room for today. If useful, start a thirty-minute Block Now session for distracting apps while you do it.
